1.explanation:
All of these files live in the “create-append-anything” feature and cooperate to support the ‘a’ shortcut:

• CreateAppendKeyboardBindings.js registers the ‘a’ key and calls the “createAppend” editor action. If it never fires off or the context passed in is invalid, nothing will happen on keyboard press.  
• CreateAppendEditorActions.js contains the implementation of that “createAppend” action: it looks up available append entries (via the context pad or rules) and, in the absence of append, should fall back to opening the create menu. A missing or incorrect fallback here causes the keypress to become a no-op.  
• AppendRules.js are used to determine whether appending (and of what shape) is permitted. If these rules aren’t consulted (or return false for those boundary‐type elements), the editor action may decide there’s nothing to append and also not trigger the create fallback.  
• AppendContextPadProvider.js and AppendMenuProvider.js register the context-pad handles and menu items for append. If the context-pad provider never registers handles for certain elements (or the menu provider fails to register a default item), the editor action logic ends up with an empty list of append options and, if its fallback logic is broken, simply does nothing.  

Fixing the bug will require ensuring the editor action always invokes the create menu when AppendRules yield no append entries and/or the ContextPad providers register a generic fallback item for elements that allow appending in principle.
1.bug_scenario: When you select an element (in this case an event sub-process) that in principle supports appending but for which no context-pad append actions are registered (so no little blue handles show up), pressing the “a” shortcut does nothing. According to the design, the “a” key should always fall back to opening the create menu when append isn’t available, but in this situation it simply is ignored.

2.explanation:
All of these modules collaborate to implement the “append” shortcut (key ‘a’) and its fall‐back to a create action. 

• CreateAppendKeyboardBindings.js: wires the ‘a’ key to invoke the append/create command.  
• CreateAppendEditorActions.js: defines the underlying editor actions (append vs. createAppend).  
• AppendContextPadProvider.js & AppendMenuProvider.js: decide what menu entries show up on the context pad; here they return empty for an Event Sub‐Process, so no append action is triggered.  
• AppendRules.js: contains rules determining whether append is allowed on a given element at all.  
• util/OptionsUtil.js: consolidates default options for append and create flows.  
• BpmnAutoPlace.js & BpmnAutoPlaceUtil.js: perform the actual auto‐place logic when an append or create action is fired.  

The missing fallback path lives in the keyboard binding / editor action layer: when no append entries exist, the code never calls the createAppend path. Fixing this requires updating CreateAppendKeyboardBindings.js and its companion action/providers so that on “a” it always falls back to create, regardless of context pad contents.
2.bug_scenario: When working on an Event Sub‐Process (or any BPMN element that in principle supports append) the context pad has no concrete append entries (the little ‘+’ menu is empty). Hitting the “a” keyboard shortcut in that situation—by design it should fall back to opening the create‐append menu or auto‐place a new shape—does nothing. Instead of defaulting to a create action, the binding only fires when explicit append entries exist.
